subject.title: feat: allow standalone MCP Apps to use bound tools and resources

question: Should ticketed standalone MCP App views be allowed to invoke the owning server’s app-visible tools and resources under the proposed view-bound authorization contract?
rationale: The patch is intentionally adding capability across a browser-to-gateway security boundary; code review can assess mechanics, but cannot choose the permanent authority policy or acceptable residual risk without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve the scoped bridge
options.body: Accept live ticketed views as a supported least-privilege operation surface after a current-head rebase and repeat conformance proof.

options.title: Keep standalone views read-only
options.body: Retain the existing rendering-only ticket model until a broader product or channel-launch design is approved.

options.title: Narrow the authority further
options.body: Approve only a smaller resource or tool subset if maintainers want a stricter first deployment boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped bridge
recommendation.body: Accept live ticketed views as a supported least-privilege operation surface after a current-head rebase and repeat conformance proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest documented history across the feature proposal, implementation, and adjacent MCP App security hardening, though final policy acceptance requires repository maintainer judgment.
